facts.problem: some booked customers don't turn up, so a barber's chair sits empty at a busy time
facts.cause: the only confirmation is an email sent at booking, often days earlier, and it gets buried under other notifications
facts.solution: a text the day before that the customer can reply to if they can't make it
facts.outcome: when someone replies, the shop can offer that chair time to someone on the walk-in list

missing_primitives.name: walk_in_list
missing_primitives.why: The outcome mentions a walk-in list, and there is no list primitive. One present person near the open calendar slot stands in for someone on that list. The narration says 'walk-in' so the meaning stays clear.

Chair time can go to a walk-in

checks: Fixed the c1 label problem: the chair is now 2x1 across row 1 only, so r2c1, r2c2 and r3c2 are all free. The calendar (r3c1) and the walk-in person (r3c3) have a free cell between them (r3c2) and free cells above (r2c1, r2c2). The label is also shorter: 'Offer to a walk-in' is 18 characters.

All facts come only from the brief. There are no invented prices, times, statistics or guarantees, and no digits in on-screen text. The only number is days_before 1, which is the brief's 'day before'.
None of the forbidden words appear (guarantee, always, never, best, lowest, save).
No em or en dashes are used.
Every essential fact is present, so there are no questions.
The narration was drafted in the owner's voice. It is about 37 words, a little over the target, because the fix needs both the reply and the walk-in offer.
The outcome is shown only as possible. The calendar becomes 'available', the chair stays empty, the narration keeps 'can', and nothing is shown as rebooked or occupied.
Each item is drawn once. The email, the text and the reply all appear on one phone, and the burying uses 'bury'.
There are 4 objects. The chair (2x1) and the phone (1x2) are the large story carriers. The calendar and the walk-in person are 1x1 supporting objects.
Nothing overlaps: chair r1c1 to r1c2, phone r1c3 to r2c3, calendar r3c1, walk-in person r3c3.
The chair's callout works because the chair is in row 1, and r2c1 and r2c2 below it are also free.
Every event's 'on' value is either 'start' or one word copied exactly from that chapter's narration. Events are listed in time order.
Each object is drawn before it changes or connects.
All text is within its limit: chapter labels 14 or fewer characters, kickers 28 or fewer, headline lines 20 or fewer, callout and label 22 or fewer, messages 34 or fewer, checklist lines 34 or fewer.
There is no primitive for the walk-in list. It is logged as non-essential, and a present person stands in for it.
